label: Synth bass 2, sampled, close and dry
audition_title: libsonare synth bass 2 vs the sampled reference
_notes: Every fourth semitone across the compass this program is probed on, 28 to 52, and no further. Both ends were rendered before the grid was written and both speak: the peaks run 0.373, 0.347, 0.334 at the low, middle and high probe notes, and the share of energy on the played key's own series is 0.978 or better at all three. A note outside the compass is left out rather than transposed, because there the reference is stretching a sample and a model fitted against it would be fitted against the sampler.
_velocities: Five. On a plucked string velocity is the pluck itself rather than a volume control, so it moves the partial stack as much as the level: on this slot velocity 32 sits -8.3 dB under velocity 100 at the middle probe note. The softest row is kept because it is the most distinct timbre the instrument has, not because the level is interesting.
_dry: Nothing to switch off, measured rather than assumed. Not one of the plugin's advertised parameters matches `reverb` with this rack loaded, and the render agrees: the note goes to the numerical floor within a fifth of a second of the key lifting, with no tail behind it. `dry` therefore has no section to act on and is left off rather than claiming an effect was disabled, which makes this a dry anchor.
_stimulus: A plucked string is stopped by the player rather than by running out, so the gate is long and the tail is short - the opposite of a voice whose interest is what follows the release. This slot does not fall under a held key - -11 dBFS a quarter of a second in and -11 at six seconds - so what its GM family calls a plucked string is here a sustained source, and the three free-decay dimensions are excused with that measurement rather than gated on a flat line. The key lifting then damps it to the numerical floor within a fifth of a second, so half a second of tail records the whole of the stop.
_calibration: From `capture.py calibrate` on this rack: the reference renders identically in real time and faster than it, the same note twice is bit-identical - so there is no round robin to put a floor under the loss - and the settle minimum is a quarter of a second. `realtime` is kept on anyway, because a note streamed late is caught only by `verify` and would otherwise be committed as a measurement.
_timbres: One, and the ladder is monotone above it, so this capture cannot move the voice past `voiced` however complete its coverage. The rack holds one slot per GM program, so there is no second of this instrument in it to disagree with, and `source_for` takes every timbre of a capture from one plugin, so a soundfont render cannot stand in as a second. What the reference buys is a measured target for `autofit` and `--diagnose` where the voice could previously only be fitted by ear.
_dimensions: Velocity only, the same split the standard kit takes: `policy.json` aims a machine-defined slot at the module on both axes, and the module holds one recording per note, so how the sound moves with velocity is the one thing its recordings cannot answer. Colour and behaviour are gated on `synth_bass_2_module`. What this capture measured before the split stays in its reference profile.
_dimensions_na: The exclusions as data, since a dimension argued only in prose reads as a gap. Coverage is read against `toneclass.canonical_dimensions`, which for a plucked string names every melodic dimension - it has a free decay, a two-stage fall, a damper and a dynamic range, and the stiff-string ladder means something - so anything not gated here has to be argued here.

dimensions_na.stereo: the slot renders dual mono: the two channels are bit-identical, so the width is zero by construction rather than by voicing
dimensions_na.decay: the slot does not decay under a held key: -11 dBFS a quarter of a second in and -11 at six seconds, so the slope a free fall would have is not in this reference
dimensions_na.aftersound: there is no free fall to have a late stage, the level being flat under a held key
dimensions_na.doubling: there is no free fall to have a prompt stage, the level being flat under a held key
dimensions_na.stretch: colour, which `policy.json` assigns to the module for a machine-defined slot on both axes. `synth_bass_2_module` gates it from the module's own recording of this tone; a bound recorded here would hold the voice to a sample library's idea of a sound the machine invented. _identity: Which product this is captured from lives in the untracked sibling `synth_bass_2.local.json`. Everything here is the method. Re-capturing needs the overlay; scoring, fitting and diagnosing read `reference/synth_bass_2.json` and need nothing.
_slots: Slot identity is measured, never taken from a name or a position. The rack is addressed by MIDI channel; this program answers on channel 8, and it was rendered at its own three probe notes before anything else was written, reading 0.978 or better of its energy on the series of the key pressed. The same renders are what say the slot rings at all: four slots of these racks hold a sample that is at the numerical floor half a second into a six-second key, and a grid written for one of those would take every measurement on silence.
